commentary:
Energy is the morning's talking point, and the story is one of unwinding war premium. Brent is limping toward its longest losing streak in over a year, hovering just under $100 as traders lean into hopes of progress in US-Iran talks and higher supply — Brent put volumes hit a record, dominated by downside protection at the $92/$93 and even $69/$70 strikes, while the call skew is the least bullish since June. WTI slipped 0.6% to $89.95 with open interest at its lowest since April last year, though products are diverging: gasoil ripped 4.3% and RBOB gained 1.1% on a gasoline crack at its firmest since mid-August, a reminder that Gulf disruption is still biting refined-product balances even as crude deflates.

The macro backdrop is a hawkish-Fed, strong-dollar regime — the greenback hit its highest since July after the Fed's first hike in three years, with traders now hedging a shallower tightening cycle than priced. That dollar strength is squeezing the metals complex: gold fell 0.6%, silver 1.3%, platinum nearly 2%, with the whole precious space trading as a rates story. Grains also buckled under the firmer dollar, with corn and both wheats off more than 1%. In rates, the eurozone's punchy composite PMI beat (53.1 vs 51.7 expected) knocked Bunds and OATs lower, while a soft UK print pressured sterling; Treasuries were marginally bid.

Equity futures are flat-to-heavy in the West, but the Nikkei surged 2.3% and KOSPI 1.4% ahead of the Trump-Xi summit — with PBoC pre-holiday liquidity injections adding support.
